cublasLtClusterShape_t.doc: `cublasLtClusterShape_t` is an enumerated type used to configure thread block cluster dimensions. Thread block clusters add an optional hierarchical level and are made up of thread blocks. Similar to thread blocks, these can be one, two, or three-dimensional. See also [Thread Block Clusters](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#thread-block-clusters).

cublasLtEpilogue_t.doc:
The `cublasLtEpilogue_t` is an enum type to set the postprocessing options for the epilogue.

**NOTES:**.

cublasLtHandle_t.doc: The `cublasLtHandle_t` type is a pointer type to an opaque structure holding the cuBLASLt library context. Use `cublasLtCreate` to initialize the cuBLASLt library context and return a handle to an opaque structure holding the cuBLASLt library context, and use `cublasLtDestroy` to destroy a previously created cuBLASLt library context descriptor and release the resources.

cublasLtLoggerCallback_t.doc: `cublasLtLoggerCallback_t` is a callback function pointer type. A callback function can be set using `cublasLtLoggerSetCallback`.

functionName.doc: The name of the API that logged this message.

cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` is an opaque structure holding the description of the matrix multiplication algorithm. This structure can be trivially serialized and later restored for use with the same version of cuBLAS library to save on selecting the right configuration again.

cublasLtMatmulAlgoCapAttributes_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulAlgoCapAttributes_t` enumerates matrix multiplication algorithm capability attributes that can be retrieved from an initialized `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptor using `cublasLtMatmulAlgoCapGetAttribute`.

cublasLtMatmulAlgoConfigAttributes_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulAlgoConfigAttributes_t` is an enumerated type that contains the configuration attributes for cuBLASLt matrix multiply algorithms. The configuration attributes are algorithm-specific, and can be set. The attributes configuration of a given algorithm should agree with its capability attributes. Use `cublasLtMatmulAlgoConfigGetAttribute` and `cublasLtMatmulAlgoConfigSetAttribute` to get and set the attribute value of a matmul algorithm descriptor.

cublasLtMatmulDesc_t.doc: The `cublasLtMatmulDesc_t` is a pointer to an opaque structure holding the description of the matrix multiplication operation `cublasLtMatmul`. A descriptor can be created by calling `cublasLtMatmulDescCreate` and destroyed by calling `cublasLtMatmulDescDestroy`.

cublasLtMatmulDescAttributes_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulDescAttributes_t` is a descriptor structure containing the attributes that define the specifics of the matrix multiply operation. Use `cublasLtMatmulDescGetAttribute` and `cublasLtMatmulDescSetAttribute` to get and set the attribute value of a matmul descriptor.

cublasLtMatmulHeuristicResult_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulHeuristicResult_t` is a descriptor that holds the configured matrix multiplication algorithm descriptor and its runtime properties.

cublasLtMatmulInnerShape_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulInnerShape_t` is an enumerated type used to configure various aspects of the internal kernel design. This does not impact the CUDA grid size.

cublasLtMatmulPreference_t.doc: The `cublasLtMatmulPreference_t` is a pointer to an opaque structure holding the description of the preferences for `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` configuration. Use `cublasLtMatmulPreferenceCreate` to create one instance of the descriptor and `cublasLtMatmulPreferenceDestroy` to destroy a previously created descriptor and release the resources.

cublasLtMatmulPreferenceAttributes_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulPreferenceAttributes_t` is an enumerated type used to apply algorithm search preferences while fine-tuning the heuristic function. Use `cublasLtMatmulPreferenceGetAttribute` and `cublasLtMatmulPreferenceSetAttribute` to get and set the attribute value of a matmul preference descriptor.

cublasLtMatmulSearch_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulSearch_t` is an enumerated type that contains the attributes for heuristics search type.

cublasLtMatmulTile_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulTile_t` is an enumerated type used to set the tile size in `rows x columns.` See also [CUTLASS: Fast Linear Algebra in CUDA C++](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://devblogs.nvidia.com/cutlass-linear-algebra-cuda/&sa=D&ust=1543610995532000&usg=AFQjCNE3tHlNsXDOnOhbVeeH1uXWQFLzLA).

cublasLtMatmulStages_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulStages_t` is an enumerated type used to configure the size and number of shared memory buffers where input elements are staged. Number of staging buffers defines kernel’s pipeline depth.

cublasLtNumericalImplFlags_t.doc:
`cublasLtNumericalImplFlags_t`: a set of bit-flags that can be specified to select implementation details that may affect numerical behavior of algorithms.

Flags below can be combined using the bit OR operator “|”.

cublasLtMatrixLayout_t.doc: The `cublasLtMatrixLayout_t` is a pointer to an opaque structure holding the description of a matrix layout. Use `cublasLtMatrixLayoutCreate` or `cublasLtGroupedMatrixLayoutCreate` to create one instance of the descriptor and `cublasLtMatrixLayoutDestroy` to destroy a previously created descriptor and release the resources.

cublasLtMatrixLayoutAttribute_t.doc: `cublasLtMatrixLayoutAttribute_t` is a descriptor structure containing the attributes that define the details of the matrix operation. Use `cublasLtMatrixLayoutGetAttribute` and `cublasLtMatrixLayoutSetAttribute` to get and set the attribute value of a matrix layout descriptor.

cublasLtIntegerWidth_t.doc: Experimental: `cublasLtIntegerWidth_t` is an enumerated type used to indicate the width of integers in the dimensions arrays of a grouped matrix.

cublasLtMatrixTransformDesc_t.doc: The `cublasLtMatrixTransformDesc_t` is a pointer to an opaque structure holding the description of a matrix transformation operation. Use `cublasLtMatrixTransformDescCreate` to create one instance of the descriptor and `cublasLtMatrixTransformDescDestroy` to destroy a previously created descriptor and release the resources.

cublasLtMatrixTransformDescAttributes_t.doc: `cublasLtMatrixTransformDescAttributes_t` is a descriptor structure containing the attributes that define the specifics of the matrix transform operation. Use `cublasLtMatrixTransformDescGetAttribute` and `cublasLtMatrixTransformDescSetAttribute` to set the attribute value of a matrix transform descriptor.

cublasLtOrder_t.doc: `cublasLtOrder_t` is an enumerated type used to indicate the data ordering of the matrix.

cublasLtPointerMode_t.doc: `cublasLtPointerMode_t` is an enumerated type used to set the pointer mode for the scaling factors `alpha` and `beta`.

cublasLtPointerModeMask_t.doc: `cublasLtPointerModeMask_t` is an enumerated type used to define and query the pointer mode capability.

cublasLtReductionScheme_t.doc: `cublasLtReductionScheme_t` is an enumerated type used to specify a reduction scheme for the portions of the dot-product calculated in parallel (i.e., “split - K”).

cublasLtMatmulMatrixScale_t.doc: `cublasLtMatmulMatrixScale_t` is an enumerated type used to specify scaling mode that defines how scaling factor pointers are interpreted.

cublasLtEmulationDesc_t.doc: cublasLtEmulationDesc_t is a pointer to an opaque structure holding the emulation descriptor. Use `cublasLtEmulationDescCreate` to create a new emulation descriptor, and `cublasLtEmulationDescDestroy` to destroy it and release the resources.

cublasLtEmulationDescAttributes_t.doc: cublasLtEmulationDescAttributes_t is an enumerated type used to configure floating point emulation parameters. See Floating Point Emulation documentation for more details.

cublasLtCreate.doc:
This function initializes the cuBLASLt library and creates a handle to an opaque structure holding the cuBLASLt library context. It allocates light hardware resources on the host and device, and must be called prior to making any other cuBLASLt library calls.

The cuBLASLt library context is tied to the current CUDA device. To use the library on multiple devices, one cuBLASLt handle must be created for each device. Furthermore, the device must be set as the current before invoking cuBLASLt functions with a handle tied to that device.

See also: cuBLAS Context.

See `cublasStatus_t` for a complete list of valid return codes.

lightHandle.doc: Pointer to the allocated cuBLASLt handle for the created cuBLASLt context.

CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED.doc:
The cuBLASLt library was not initialized. This usually happens:
  - when `cublasLtCreate` is not called first
  - an error in the CUDA Runtime API called by the cuBLASLt routine, or an error in the hardware setup.

CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED.doc:
Resource allocation failed inside the cuBLASLt library. This is usually caused by a `cudaMalloc()` failure.

To correct: prior to the function call, deallocate the previously allocated memory as much as possible.

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: `lighthandle` is NULL.

cublasLtDestroy.doc:
This function releases hardware resources used by the cuBLASLt library. This function is usually the last call with a particular handle to the cuBLASLt library. Because `cublasLtCreate` allocates some internal resources and the release of those resources by calling `cublasLtDestroy` will implicitly call `cudaDeviceSynchronize()`, it is recommended to minimize the number of times these functions are called.

See `cublasStatus_t` for a complete list of valid return codes.

lightHandle.doc: Pointer to the cuBLASLt handle to be destroyed.

CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS.doc: The cuBLASLt context was successfully destroyed.

CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED.doc: The cuBLASLt library was not initialized.

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: `lightHandle` is NULL.

cublasLtDisableCpuInstructionsSetMask.doc:

The function takes precedence over the `CUBLASLT_DISABLE_CPU_INSTRUCTIONS_MASK` environment variable.

 `mask` – the flags combined with bitwise `OR(|)` operator that specify which CPU instructions should not be used.

Supported flags:

 the previous value of the `mask`.

D.doc: Pointer to the GPU memory associated with the descriptor `Ddesc`.

stream.doc: The CUDA stream where all the GPU work will be submitted.

CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED.doc: If cuBLASLt handle has not been initialized.

This function performs the correctness check on the matrix multiply algorithm descriptor for the matrix multiply operation `cublasLtMatmul` function with the given input matrices A, B and C, and the output matrix D. It checks whether the descriptor is supported on the current device, and returns the result containing the required workspace and the calculated wave count.

See `cublasStatus_t` for a complete list of valid return codes.

cublasLtMatmulAlgoCheckForStream.doc:
This function performs the correctness check on the matrix multiply algorithm descriptor for the matrix multiply operation `cublasLtMatmul` function with the given input matrices A, B and C, and the output matrix D. It checks whether the descriptor is supported on the current device and execution context (specified by the stream), and returns the result containing the required workspace and the calculated wave count.

If the stream is associated with a Green Context (a CUDA execution context that provides access to a subset of GPU resources), the check reflects the SM count and resource constraints of that context, not the full device. cublasLtMatrixTransform.doc:
This function computes the matrix transformation operation on the input matrices A and B, to produce the output matrix C, according to the below operation:

`C = alpha*transformation(A) + beta*transformation(B),`

where `A`, `B` are input matrices, and `alpha` and `beta` are input scalars. The transformation operation is defined by the `transformDesc` pointer. This function can be used to change the memory order of data or to scale and shift the values.

See `cublasStatus_t` for a complete list of valid return codes.

cublasXtHandle_t.doc: The `cublasXtHandle_t` type is a pointer type to an opaque structure holding the cuBLASXt API context. The cuBLASXt API context must be initialized using `cublasXtCreate` and the returned handle must be passed to all subsequent cuBLASXt API function calls. The context should be destroyed at the end using `cublasXtDestroy`.

cublasXtOpType_t.doc: The `cublasOpType_t` enumerates the four possible types supported by BLAS routines. This enum is used as parameters of the routines `cublasXtSetCpuRoutine` and `cublasXtSetCpuRatio` to setup the hybrid configuration.

cublasXtBlasOp_t.doc: The `cublasXtBlasOp_t` type enumerates the BLAS3 or BLAS-like routine supported by cuBLASXt API. This enum is used as parameters of the routines `cublasXtSetCpuRoutine` and `cublasXtSetCpuRatio` to setup the hybrid configuration.

cublasXtPinningMemMode_t.doc: The type is used to enable or disable the Pinning Memory mode through the routine `cubasMgSetPinningMemMode`.

CUBLASXT_PINNING_DISABLED.doc: the Pinning Memory mode is disabled.

CUBLASXT_PINNING_ENABLED.doc: the Pinning Memory mode is enabled.

cublasXtCreate.doc: This function initializes the cuBLASXt API and creates a handle to an opaque structure holding the cuBLASXt API context. It allocates hardware resources on the host and device and must be called prior to making any other cuBLASXt API calls.

CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED.doc: the resources could not be allocated.

CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: cuBLASXt API is only supported on 64-bit platform.

cublasXtDestroy.doc: This function releases hardware resources used by the cuBLASXt API context. The release of GPU resources may be deferred until the application exits. This function is usually the last call with a particular handle to the cuBLASXt API.

cublasXtDeviceSelect.doc: This function allows the user to provide the number of GPU devices and their respective Ids that will participate to the subsequent cuBLASXt API Math function calls. This function will create a cuBLAS context for every GPU provided in that list. Currently the device configuration is static and cannot be changed between Math function calls. In that regard, this function should be called only once after `cublasXtCreate`. To be able to run multiple configurations, multiple cuBLASXt API contexts should be created.
cublasXtDeviceSelect.signature: cublasXtDeviceSelect(cublasXtHandle_t handle, int nbDevices, int deviceId[])

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: Access to at least one of the device could not be done or a cuBLAS context could not be created on at least one of the device.

CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED.doc: Some resources could not be allocated.

cublasXtSetBlockDim.doc: This function allows the user to set the block dimension used for the tiling of the matrices for the subsequent Math function calls. Matrices are split in square tiles of blockDim x blockDim dimension. This function can be called anytime and will take effect for the following Math function calls. The block dimension should be chosen in a way to optimize the math operation and to make sure that the PCI transfers are well overlapped with the computation.

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: blockDim <= 0.

cublasXtGetBlockDim.doc: This function allows the user to query the block dimension used for the tiling of the matrices.

cublasXtSetCpuRoutine.doc: This function allows the user to provide a CPU implementation of the corresponding BLAS routine. This function can be used with the function `cublasXtSetCpuRatio` to define an hybrid computation between the CPU and the GPUs. Currently the hybrid feature is only supported for the xGEMM routines.
cublasXtSetCpuRoutine.signature: cublasXtSetCpuRoutine(cublasXtHandle_t handle, cublasXtBlasOp_t blasOp, cublasXtOpType_t type, void *blasFunctor)

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: blasOp or type define an invalid combination.

CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: CPU-GPU Hybridization for that routine is not supported.

cublasXtSetCpuRatio.doc: This function allows the user to define the percentage of workload that should be done on a CPU in the context of an hybrid computation. This function can be used with the function `cublasXtSetCpuRoutine` to define an hybrid computation between the CPU and the GPUs. Currently the hybrid feature is only supported for the xGEMM routines.
cublasXtSetCpuRatio.signature: cublasXtSetCpuRatio(cublasXtHandle_t handle, cublasXtBlasOp_t blasOp, cublasXtOpType_t type, float ratio)

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: blasOp or type define an invalid combination.

CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: CPU-GPU Hybridization for that routine is not supported.

cublasXtSetPinningMemMode.doc: This function allows the user to enable or disable the Pinning Memory mode. When enabled, the matrices passed in subsequent cuBLASXt API calls will be pinned/unpinned using the CUDART routine `cudaHostRegister()` and `cudaHostUnregister()` respectively if the matrices are not already pinned. If a matrix happened to be pinned partially, it will also not be pinned. Pinning the memory improve PCI transfer performance and allows to overlap PCI memory transfer with computation. However pinning/unpinning the memory take some time which might not be amortized. It is advised that the user pins the memory on its own using `cudaMallocHost()` or `cudaHostRegister()` and unpin it when the computation sequence is completed. By default, the Pinning Memory mode is disabled.

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: the mode value is different from [`cublasXtPinningMemMode_t::CUBLASXT_PINNING_DISABLED`] and [`cublasXtPinningMemMode_t::CUBLASXT_PINNING_ENABLED`].

cublasXtGetPinningMemMode.doc: This function allows the user to query the Pinning Memory mode. By default, the Pinning Memory mode is disabled.

cublasXt<t>gemm.doc:
This function performs the matrix-matrix multiplication:

$$
C = \alpha\text{op}(A)\text{op}(B) + \beta C
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars, and $A$, $B$ and $C$ are matrices stored in column-major format with dimensions $\text{op}(A)$ $m \times k$, $\text{op}(B)$ $k \times n$ and $C$ $m \times n$, respectively. Also, for matrix $A$:

$$
\text{op}(A) = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
A & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_N}$}} \\\\
A^{T} & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_T}$}} \\\\
A^{H} & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_C}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

and $\text{op}(B)$ is defined similarly for matrix $B$.

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[sgemm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/sgemm.f), [dgemm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/dgemm.f), [cgemm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/cgemm.f), [zgemm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/zgemm.f).

handle.doc: handle to the cuBLASXt API context.

transa.doc: operation op(`A`) that is non- or (conj.) transpose.

transb.doc: operation op(`B`) that is non- or (conj.) transpose.

m.doc: number of rows of matrix op(`A`) and `C`.

n.doc: number of columns of matrix op(`B`) and `C`.

k.doc: number of columns of op(`A`) and rows of op(`B`).

A.doc: <*type*> array of dimensions `lda x k` with `lda >= max(1, m)` if `transa == CUBLAS_OP_N` and `lda x m` with `lda >= max(1, k)` otherwise.

lda.doc: leading dimension of two-dimensional array used to store the matrix `A`.

B.doc: <*type*> array of dimension `ldb x n` with `ldb >= max(1, k)` if `transb == CUBLAS_OP_N` and `ldb x k` with `ldb >= max(1, n)` otherwise.

ldb.doc: leading dimension of two-dimensional array used to store matrix `B`.

beta.doc: <*type*> scalar used for multiplication. If `beta == 0`, `C` does not have to be a valid input.

C.doc: <*type*> array of dimensions `ldc x n` with `ldc >= max(1, m)`.

ldc.doc: leading dimension of a two-dimensional array used to store the matrix `C`.

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: the parameters `m,n,k<0`.

CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED.doc: the function failed to launch on the GPU.

cublasXt<t>hemm.doc:
This function performs the Hermitian matrix-matrix multiplication:

$$
C = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
{\alpha AB + \beta C} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_LEFT}$}} \\\\
{\alpha BA + \beta C} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_RIGHT}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

where $A$ is a Hermitian matrix stored in lower or upper mode, $B$ and $C$ are $m \times n$ matrices, and $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars.

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[chemm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/chemm.f), [zhemm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/zhemm.f).

handle.doc: handle to the cuBLASXt API context.

side.doc: indicates if matrix `A` is on the left or right of `B`.

uplo.doc: indicates if matrix `A` lower or upper part is stored, the other Hermitian part is not referenced and is inferred from the stored elements.

m.doc: number of rows of matrix `C` and `B`, with matrix `A` sized accordingly.

n.doc: number of columns of matrix `C` and `B`, with matrix `A` sized accordingly.

A.doc: <*type*> array of dimension `lda x m` with `lda >= max(1, m)` if `side = CUBLAS_SIDE_LEFT` and `lda x n` with `lda >= max(1, n)` otherwise. The imaginary parts of the diagonal elements are assumed to be zero.

lda.doc: leading dimension of two-dimensional array used to store matrix `A`.

B.doc: <*type*> array of dimension `ldb x n` with `ldb >= max(1, m)`.

ldb.doc: leading dimension of two-dimensional array used to store matrix `B`.

beta.doc: <*type*> scalar used for multiplication, if `beta == 0` then `C` does not have to be a valid input.

C.doc: <*type*> array of dimensions `ldc x n` with `ldc >= max(1, m)`.

ldc.doc: leading dimension of two-dimensional array used to store matrix `C`.

CUBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: the parameters `m < 0` or `n < 0`.

CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED.doc: the function failed to launch on the GPU.

cublasXt<t>symm.doc:
This function performs the symmetric matrix-matrix multiplication:

$$
C = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
{\alpha AB + \beta C} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_LEFT}$}} \\\\
{\alpha BA + \beta C} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_RIGHT}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

where $A$ is a symmetric matrix stored in lower or upper mode, $A$ and $A$ are $m \times n$ matrices, and $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars.

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[ssymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ssymm.f), [dsymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/dsymm.f), [csymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/csymm.f), [zsymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/zsymm.f).

cublasXt<t>syrk.doc:
This function performs the symmetric rank- $k$ update:

$$
C = \alpha\text{op}(A)\text{op}(A)^{T} + \beta C
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars, $C$ is a symmetric matrix stored in lower or upper mode, and $A$ is a matrix with dimensions $\text{op}(A)$ $n \times k$. Also, for matrix $A$:

$$
\text{op}(A) = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
A & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_N}$}} \\\\
A^{T} & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_T}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[ssyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ssyrk.f), [dsyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/dsyrk.f), [csyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/csyrk.f), [zsyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/zsyrk.f).

handle.doc: handle to the cuBLASXt API context.

uplo.doc: indicates if matrix `C` lower or upper part is stored, the other symmetric part is not referenced and is inferred from the stored elements.

trans.doc: operation op(`A`) that is non- or transpose.

n.doc: number of rows of matrix op(`A`) and `C`.

k.doc: number of columns of matrix op(`A`).

A.doc: <*type*> array of dimension `lda x k` with `lda >= max(1, n)` if `trans == CUBLAS_OP_N` and `lda x n` with `lda >= max(1, k)` otherwise.

lda.doc: leading dimension of two-dimensional array used to store matrix A.

beta.doc: <*type*> scalar used for multiplication, if `beta == 0` then `C` does not have to be a valid input.

C.doc: <*type*> array of dimension `ldc x n`, with `ldc >= max(1, n)`.

cublasXt<t>syr2k.doc:
This function performs the symmetric rank- $2k$ update:

$$
C = \alpha(\text{op}(A)\text{op}(B)^{T} + \text{op}(B)\text{op}(A)^{T}) + \beta C
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars, $C$ is a symmetric matrix stored in lower or upper mode, and $A$ and $B$ are matrices with dimensions $\text{op}(A)$ $n \times k$ and $\text{op}(B)$ $n \times k$, respectively. Also, for matrix $A$ and $B$:

$$
\text{op(}A\text{) and op(}B\text{)} = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
{A\text{ and }B} & {\text{if }\textsf{trans == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_N}$}} \\\\
{A^{T}\text{ and }B^{T}} & {\text{if }\textsf{trans == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_T}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

cublasXt<t>syrkx.doc:
This function performs a variation of the symmetric rank- $k$ update:

$$
C = \alpha(\text{op}(A)\text{op}(B)^{T} + \beta C
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars, $C$ is a symmetric matrix stored in lower or upper mode, and $A$ and $B$ are matrices with dimensions $\text{op}(A)$ $n \times k$ and $\text{op}(B)$ $n \times k$, respectively. Also, for matrix $A$ and $B$:

$$
\text{op(}A\text{) and op(}B\text{)} = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
{A\text{ and }B} & {\text{if }\textsf{trans == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_N}$}} \\\\
{A^{T}\text{ and }B^{T}} & {\text{if }\textsf{trans == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_T}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

This routine can be used when B is in such way that the result is guaranteed to be symmetric. A usual example is when the matrix B is a scaled form of the matrix A : this is equivalent to B being the product of the matrix A and a diagonal matrix.

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[ssyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ssyrk.f), [dsyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/dsyrk.f), [csyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/csyrk.f), [zsyrk()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/zsyrk.f) and

cublasXt<t>trsm.doc:
This function solves the triangular linear system with multiple right-hand-sides:

$$
\left\\{ \begin{matrix}
{\text{op}(A)X = \alpha B} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_LEFT}$}} \\\\
{X\text{op}(A) = \alpha B} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_RIGHT}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

where $A$ is a triangular matrix stored in lower or upper mode with or without the main diagonal, $X$ and $B$ are $m \times n$ matrices, and $\alpha$ is a scalar. Also, for matrix $A$:

$$
\text{op}(A) = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
A & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_N}$}} \\\\
A^{T} & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_T}$}} \\\\
A^{H} & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_C}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

The solution $X$ overwrites the right-hand-sides $B$ on exit.

No test for singularity or near-singularity is included in this function.

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[strsm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/strsm.f), [dtrsm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/dtrsm.f), [ctrsm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ctrsm.f), [ztrsm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ztrsm.f).

cublasXt<t>trmm.doc:
This function performs the triangular matrix-matrix multiplication:

$$
C = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
{\alpha\text{op}(A)B} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_LEFT}$}} \\\\
{\alpha B\text{op}(A)} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_RIGHT}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

where $A$ is a triangular matrix stored in lower or upper mode with or without the main diagonal, $B$ and $C$ are $m \times n$ matrix, and $\alpha$ is a scalar. Also, for matrix $A$:

$$
\text{op}(A) = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
A & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_N}$}} \\\\
A^{T} & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_T}$}} \\\\
A^{H} & {\text{if }\textsf{transa == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_OP_C}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

Notice that in order to achieve better parallelism, similarly to the cublas API, cuBLASXt API differs from the BLAS API for this routine. The BLAS API assumes an in-place implementation (with results written back to B), while the cuBLASXt API assumes an out-of-place implementation (with results written into C). The application can still obtain the in-place functionality of BLAS in the cuBLASXt API by passing the address of the matrix B in place of the matrix C. No other overlapping in the input parameters is supported.

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[strmm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/strmm.f), [dtrmm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/dtrmm.f), [ctrmm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ctrmm.f), [ztrmm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ztrmm.f).

cublasXt<t>spmm.doc:
This function performs the symmetric packed matrix-matrix multiplication:

$$
C = \left\\{ \begin{matrix}
{\alpha AB + \beta C} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_LEFT}$}} \\\\
{\alpha BA + \beta C} & {\text{if }\textsf{side == $\mathrm{CUBLAS_SIDE_RIGHT}$}} \\\\
\end{matrix} \right.
$$

where $A$ is a $n \times n$ symmetric matrix stored in packed format, $B$ and $C$ are $m \times n$ matrices, and $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars.

If `uplo == CUBLAS_FILL_MODE_LOWER` then the elements in the lower triangular part of the symmetric matrix $A$ are packed together column by column without gaps, so that the element $A(i,j)$ is stored in the memory location `AP[i+((2*n-j+1)*j)/2]` for $j = 1,\ldots,n$ and $i \geq j$. Consequently, the packed format requires only $\frac{n(n + 1)}{2}$ elements for storage.

If `uplo == CUBLAS_FILL_MODE_UPPER` then the elements in the upper triangular part of the symmetric matrix $A$ are packed together column by column without gaps, so that the element $A(i,j)$ is stored in the memory location `AP[i+(j*(j+1))/2]` for $j = 1,\ldots,n$ and $i \leq j$. Consequently, the packed format requires only $\frac{n(n + 1)}{2}$ elements for storage.

For references please refer to NETLIB documentation:

[ssymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/ssymm.f), [dsymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/dsymm.f), [csymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/csymm.f), [zsymm()](http://www.netlib.org/blas/zsymm.f).
